summary: instr returns the one-based position of the first matching substring, or zero if it is absent.
documentation: instr returns the one-based position of the first matching substring, or zero if it is absent. Text matching is literal; NULL arguments produce NULL.
inputs: A text value and a literal search substring.
returns: A one-based integer position, zero, or NULL.
caution: SQLite positions differ from JavaScript indexOf: the first position is 1, and the missing marker is 0 rather than -1.
scenarios: Locate a separator in an imported reference.
Find the first literal token in a report field.
Check whether a documented marker appears before extracting text.
title: Locate a stored separator
problem: From records(id INTEGER, label TEXT), return id and instr(label, ':') as position, ordered by id. Preserve NULL for a NULL label; return zero when no colon exists.
goal: Use instr() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Use instr and its one-based convention.
